A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 19-page versions of OpenEstimate. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material that was moved or renumbered.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, statistical-baseline comparisons, calibration analyses, and inference-setting ablations in Section 3 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations, revised win rates and calibration results, CRPS comparisons, and ablation results in Section 3 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 and Appendix A.2 replace specified Gaussian/Beta priors with model-selected Gaussian, Beta, or log-normal priors. All three elicitation protocols now request distribution selection, changing the inference procedure and outputs. The statistic-generation algorithm remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Table 1 retains the same 178 estimation targets: 43 Glassdoor, 61 Pitchbook, and 74 NHANES statistics, with the same marginal and conditional coverage. New illustrative examples inside prompts do not establish additional evaluated datasets or domains.

E2.justification: The overall model roster and statistical baselines remain unchanged. Within the uncertainty-accuracy comparison, however, v2 Figure 5 includes Llama-3-8B for Glassdoor and NHANES, whereas v1 Figure 6 shows it only for Pitchbook. It already appeared in v1's other calibration analyses, so this is a limited expansion within a reported comparison.

E3.justification: Accuracy evaluation changes from distribution modes to means for both LM predictions and statistical baselines. CRPS ratios replace quartile ECE as the principal distributional evaluation metric, while ECE remains in Appendix A.2. These materially revise the reported evaluation protocol; the baseline sample sizes and stated temperature/reasoning-effort settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 extends the retained elicitation, temperature/reasoning-effort, and system-prompt ablations with CRPS results. This adds a distributional-scoring perspective to the sensitivity analyses. The underlying ablation questions and the coverage and uncertainty-accuracy diagnostics remain; moving the elicitation figure into the appendix is not a new study.

E5.justification: The main calibration-score comparison changes from ECE bars with error bars in v1 Figure 3 to CRPS point estimates without intervals in v2 Table 3. Both retain 95% confidence intervals for accuracy and per-quartile binomial tests at p < 0.05. Neither version supplies explicit seed or repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: Results change extensively. Table 2's posterior win rates at N=30 change from 45.7% to 70.5% for Glassdoor and from 56.7% to 81.6% for Pitchbook. Figure 2 changes numerical scores and rankings; calibration and ablation plots also contain revised outcomes, and Table 3 adds CRPS ratios. Given the changed elicitation and metrics, these are replacement results rather than demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 2.3.1 revises the formal MAE definitions from deviations of distribution modes to deviations of means. Section 2.3.2 introduces CRPS and its baseline-normalized score. The quartile ECE definition is retained in the appendix, and the Bayesian update equation and statistic-generation mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution and finding that current models struggle remain. The abstract removes the claim that elicitation modestly improves performance and now emphasizes approximately five-sample prior value, posterior usefulness, and weak confidence-accuracy relationships. Posterior usefulness was already reported in v1, so this is a limited revision of headline conclusions rather than an entirely new contribution.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 replaces v1's interpretation that elicitation improves calibration through increased uncertainty with the conclusion that none of the tested settings has a consequential effect. v2 also adds CRPS-based interpretations of model size and domain differences, identifies Glassdoor underconfidence in Figure 4, and removes the Gaussian/Beta restriction from the limitations. These substantially revise the paper's explanatory conclusions.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 substantially replaces the full prompt specifications. It adds distribution-type output tags, detailed log-space parameter instructions and checks, explicit unit-conversion warnings, and worked quantile and log-normal examples. These materially change the information available for reproducing elicitation. The repository access information and stated model inference settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds Huynh et al. (2025) on LLM-based counterfactual data augmentation and Selby et al. (2025) on parametric prior elicitation. It explicitly distinguishes OpenEstimate from these approaches, especially through derived statistics and direct accuracy/calibration evaluation. The broader related-work organization remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and benchmark-description sections are extensively rewritten, including a systematic shift from 'variables' toward 'derived conditional statistics.' The ablation discussion is substantially condensed, appendix prompts are rewritten, and acknowledgments are added. This is extensive language and narrative revision despite retaining the main section order.

P2.justification: v1's main ECE bar chart is removed and v2 adds the CRPS table. All three ablation displays gain CRPS panels, several plot axes and scales change, and Table 2 is reformatted. The elicitation analysis moves into the appendix and other figures are relocated. Figure 1's artwork is retained despite its changed placement and caption.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 adds useful CRPS evaluation and more explicit distribution-selection and log-space instructions. However, revised evidence is not consistently reconciled with conclusions: Figure 3 shows every Glassdoor first-quartile frequency below 25%, yet retains the blanket overestimation claim. Section 3.2 also dismisses consequential setting effects despite Figure 6 reporting NHANES mean-variance CRPS ratios of 0.42 and 0.52 relative to direct elicitation. The added evaluation detail and weakened alignment between results and interpretation leave the net quality direction uncertain.
